metadata.description: Claude Code plugins for 3D characters and creatures built in Blender and played in Godot 4.7: bodies, rigs, moves, flesh, cloth, clothing, lighting and GDScript code intelligence.

plugins.name: godot-lsp
plugins.description: GDScript code intelligence for Claude Code. Godot ships a real language server but only listens on TCP, while Claude Code runs every LSP server over stdio — its `transport: "socket"` option is accepted and then ignored, so the two never meet. This bridges them with a dependency-free 55-line pipe, giving hover, go-to-definition, find-references, symbols and diagnostics on .gd files from the engine's own analyser, built-in class documentation included. Requires the Godot editor to be open, since the language server lives in the editor rather than the engine.

plugins.name: rig-anything
plugins.description: Rigs and animates an arbitrary Blender mesh, including shapes no template covers. Deterministic Python measures the geometry, renders let vision classify it, and the skeleton is fitted from a template where one fits or built from discovered structure where none does. It then binds with bone-heat weights, generates a looping gait for any number of legs - or a travelling wave for a body with none - and exports to glTF with the playback speed the clip's own stride implies, verified by reading the written file back. Throughout it measures rather than assumes: bone axes are probed per bone because an elbow and a knee bend opposite ways, and a rig whose pose evaluation has gone stale is made to error rather than report a confident table of zeros. Since 0.6.0 it also maps any rig to spine, neck, head, tail, legs and arms and poses it by target with IK - the engine behind animate-anything. Since 0.8.0 walks, trots and sprints are derived from ground contacts: a support plane through the measured feet, Froude-scaled stride and duty factor, and per-leg reach solved on that plane - so a sprint reaches and flies instead of replaying a walk faster - and the exporter measures speed on the planted feet. Since 0.9.0 wings are a body part: found from the skin (a sheet, not a tube) or from names, told apart as membrane or feathered, folded through the avian elbow-wrist linkage with one number, and flown - wingbeat, cruise, glide and stall speeds from wing area, span and mass, and spread, flap, glide, dive, take-off and landing clips checked for wings through the body or across the midline. Since 0.10.0 mouths are a body part: found on the skin as a cavity entering the head, given a jaw, throat and gular pouch, tongue chain and a non-deforming mouth socket, skinned by splitting the head along the lips and relaxing the split for stretch, with the gape limited to what the skin takes without folding - and bite, roar, fire-breath, swallow, engulf and purge clips checked for stretch, folded faces, rigid teeth and socket aim. Since 0.11.0 fish swim: fins are found on the skin by thickness and classified by where they attach, a fish with no rig is given a spine and a fan of ray bones per fin, and the body is laid along a travelling wave scaled by body length - stride, tail beat, cruise and burst speed from published scaling, five modes from eel to whale - with swim, sprint, glide, hover, turn, C-start and brake clips checked for tail sweep, a tailward wave and skin folding. Since 0.12.0 bodies with no front or back are an archetype of their own: the identification report measures an axis the body turns onto itself about and its order, a jellyfish, sea star, brittle star or anemone is split on the skin into a hub and a ring of appendages - loose tentacles included - and rigged with a hub, bell ribs and a chain per appendage, weighted from its parts without bone heat; a bell pulses at the rate its diameter implies and steers by closing one side harder, a sea star crawls on its tube feet in any direction, a brittle star rows behind whichever arm is nearest, and an anemone sways and retracts, every clip checked for margin closure, symmetry, tentacle lag and crossing, tips on the floor and stroke direction. Since 0.13.0 hoppers are a body plan of their own: a cricket's or rabbit's legs are found by walking up the skin from each ground contact, their joints are the corners of that walk's centreline - a heel walked separately when a flat foot hides where the shin rises, and joints buried in flesh placed from published proportions - and a pelvis-rooted rig is weighted from the parts; a rabbit hops and half-bounds on measured ankle angles through a femur-parallel-to-metatarsus leg with every planted foot at one belt speed, a cricket walks on tripods, and both jump as a launch, an engine-owned ballistic flight and a landing, checked for take-off angle, knee extension, seams and skin. Since 0.14.0 checks refuse instead of passing quietly: keys stay on the rotation channel a bone actually uses, the floor check ignores bones that carry no skin, and every clip is played back again before export - floor, skin, seam, foot slide, balance - so a layer added after authoring cannot slip through; a walk that moves nothing is refused. cycle takes max_drop, stance_width, named posture (pelvis, flex, neck in degrees toward the front, no rotation signs), an upper body solved inside the clip (arm swing opposite the legs from each arm's rest bend plane, pelvis turn and list, chest counter-rotation, a steady head) and gait styles such as elderly_shuffle, heavy and child; bake_for_game prepares a shape-keyed, over-weighted body for glTF, renders can share one scale, and a Godot MovesController reads the .moves.json manifest directly. Since 0.14.2 a jump lands: a foot whose target would put its sole through the floor stays where it was planted until the hips have risen enough for it to clear, and a clip may carry the floor it was authored against - an airborne clip is measured against the ground the engine put under it, not the origin. Since 0.15.0 export works in a later session: every set function stores each role's report on its action (and a failed role on the rig), and every engine_manifest and export_creature loads them when no reports are passed; Rigify is enabled by the fit itself under --factory-startup; and quadruped_samples makes a seeded dog with known joints. Since 0.16.0 the body map names bones by role - root, pelvis, chest, neck, head, tail, breast and butt anchors, each hand and foot, and the controls that move no skin - derived from structure and the bound skin, so a Mixamo-named rig gets the same roles as its Rigify original. Since 0.17.0 rig profiles (MPFB game engine, Rigify human and quadruped, generic, hopper) state what is known ahead of a body source - claimed roles checked against the derived ones, and the bake block bake_for_game and preflight read; bones other plugins add (jiggle, hem) stay out of the body map; and the floor, crouch and clearance checks read roles instead of their own rules. Since 0.18.0 export_character writes the .moves.json MovesController reads for bipeds and quadrupeds too, arm clearance measures the body and not the garments bound to the rig, and `adult` is a gait style. Since 0.19.0 a foot never skids along the floor: an out-of-reach foot gives up height before its place on the ground, a swinging foot is not held planted by the floor clamp or folded into the floor, every clip is checked for a grounded limb moving along the floor (floor_skid), and limbs are named as limbs (fore.L, not fore_femur.L) - the cricket exports. Since 0.20.0 slides and their recoveries pass on a Rigify biped: Slide blends through the Poser, a foot moving between two spots on the floor steps there instead of dragging, and a foot in the air is laid on the floor by its own skin. Since 0.21.0 every appendage of one radial kind gets the same bone count (the median of its kind's length-to-width ratios), so a sea star's five arms all have four bones, and radial.skin reads the written weights back to report measured coverage and vertices_unweighted. Since 0.22.0 every export writes a review sheet beside the glb: eight frames of each clip in a strip, three views and a contact montage at one scale, with the frame grown from the evaluated poses along both screen axes - so a leg that goes through the floor stays in the picture - and edge_cells counting a body that touches any edge, not only the sides. Since 0.23.0 verify.arm_swing fails a walk or run whose arm is carried out in front of hanging and never returns behind it (the pre-fix Walter walk), and export writes each idle and gait clip's arm_pose - hand_rise, elbow_flex_deg, upper_arm_deg, arm_carry_deg, arm_swing_deg per arm - into .moves.json beside clip_checks.

plugins.name: lookdev
plugins.description: Lighting and shading for Godot 4.7 scenes built with Blender assets. An agent can't judge lighting from one screenshot, so this renders a scene off-screen and measures it - exposure, clipping, key-to-fill ratio read off an 18% grey probe by surface normal, albedo range, colour cast - lints scenes and Blender materials for the mistakes that make 3D look like CG, applies lighting presets calibrated by measurement in both light-unit modes, and compares variants side by side in both orders to cancel position bias. On the Blender side it finds what the glTF exporter silently drops and what Godot ignores on import, bakes procedural materials into the layout both read, and exports with Godot-safe settings verified by reading the file back. Since 0.2.0 it carries material presets: a hair material (strand texture with alpha-thinned ends, strand normal map, anisotropy) whose settings glTF keeps as extras and a Godot addon turns into anisotropy, backlight, rim and per-face strand tangents; and detail.bake_normal_from_high bakes a sculpted high mesh's relief onto a game mesh, matched on the faces actually baked - a body with its eyes joined in still matches on the skin instead of falling back to rays in silence. Since 0.3.0 it carries a skin preset: bake.bake_material rebuilds a procedural material in place from albedo, ORM and normal maps (keeping its name, custom properties and subsurface), its skin extras make the Godot addon turn on subsurface scattering in skin mode with 1 cm transmittance and a tiling pore detail normal on UV2, and lint warns SKIN_PLASTIC on a skin with a flat albedo, one roughness, no normal detail or no subsurface.

plugins.name: animate-anything
plugins.description: Whole-body actions for any rigged creature in Blender, beyond the walk cycle: crouch, crouch walk, slide, and the recoveries out of a slide - with climb next. A walk can let feet slide a little; these cannot, because they are defined by contacts, so every pose is built from target positions rather than rotation signs. Any rig - hand-built, Rigify, or rig-anything's generic builder, whichever way its hierarchy runs - is first mapped to one body of spine, neck, head, tail, legs and arms, and actions are written in fractions of that body so one description fits a human and a rat. Poses are values that blend, so a slide recovery is simply slide -> deep crouch -> stand, and every new clip is measured to start exactly where the clip before it ends. Each clip is played back through Blender and checked: prediction against playback, planted feet, stance feet on their line, joints folding past sense, bones and skin through the floor, and balance from the skinned centre of mass. Since 0.3.0 move_set's walk, trot and sprint come from rig-anything's contact-based locomotion, with each foot's footfall schedule read back for the engine. Requires rig-anything 0.10.0 or later, which ships the code. Since 0.4.0 winged creatures fold, spread, flap, glide, dive, take off and land, and carry their wings folded through every ground action. Since 0.5.0 creatures with a modelled mouth bite, roar, breathe fire, swallow, and - for a rorqual - engulf and purge, on clips that move only the head and mouth so an engine layers them over walking and flying. Requires rig-anything 0.11.0. Since 0.6.0 fish and whales swim, with fins that fold at speed and spread to brake. Since 0.7.0 radial bodies - jellyfish, sea stars, brittle stars, anemones - pulse, crawl, row, sway and retract, with headings chosen per move because nothing has a front. Requires rig-anything 0.12.0. Since 0.8.0 hoppers hop, bound, walk and jump - a rabbit on measured ankle angles, a cricket from a cocked tibia - as launch, air and landing clips an engine joins without a seam. Since 0.9.0 people walk like who they are: posture, stance width, an upper body inside the clip and gait styles (elderly shuffle, heavy, child, brisk, relaxed) come from rig-anything's cycle, and every clip is re-checked on playback before export. Requires rig-anything 0.14.0. Since 0.9.1 it documents the floor-skid rule and limb names. Since 0.9.2 it documents how slides step and lay their feet. Since 0.10.0 a motion critic reads rig-anything's review strips: a checklist turns each clip into yes/no questions per view, and a keep-or-revert rule compares a new version against the previous one from the two .moves.json files alone. Requires rig-anything 0.23.0.

plugins.name: follow-through
plugins.description: Secondary motion for Blender assets headed to Godot 4.7 - the parts nobody keyframes: cloth, soft volumes and flesh. A router skill measures a mesh, classifies it by the dimension of what moves (strand, shell, volume) and how it is held, and types it - jello, slime, clay, a breast, a bloater's belly - from a registry of names, taught examples and anatomical zones that Claude extends by teaching, including from zones marked on labelled 2D renders mapped back onto the mesh. Cloth becomes a pinned SoftBody3D; jello, pudding, slime, clay and water balloons become lattice shape-matching bodies with squash and plasticity (Godot's Jolt soft body has no volume constraints); a rigged body's soft masses become jiggle bones sprung in a SkeletonModifier3D with exact integration and volume-keeping squash, exported with rig-anything's walk. Materials carry physical frequencies, every export is read back, and headless verifiers measure pins, stretch, volume kept, penetration, settling and each spring's frequency. Since 0.2.2 verify_volume takes clip= to choose the clip played under the flesh. Since 0.2.3 the clay ball and water balloon samples keep their face order between builds. Since 0.2.4 a flesh type's anchor names a bone role, read from rig-anything's body map, and jiggle bones are tagged ft_role. Since 0.2.5 a breast rides the chest role (where the arms attach), not the nearest spine bone. Since 0.2.6 a flesh type carries its swing limit as a share of how far the mass stands out (limit_share). Since 0.3.0 buttocks are read from the side, across the spine and thigh chains (a flesh type's lean: profile), so they land on the mass instead of the fold under it, and the butt's limit_share is 0.9. Since 0.4.0 a flesh chain's first ring, and its last built ring when the chain is searched to its end, fit their lean envelope from wall vertices only, so a crotch cap no longer skews the torso's lean envelope (the sample Figure's belly and breasts land on their masses and its false love handles are gone), and heat maps draw a profile-read buttock from its profile, not its rings. Since 0.5.0 hanging strands - a ponytail, long hair - get a chain of bones down their centreline, sprung in Godot in fixed substeps against an ellipsoid head and neck capsules and measured by a headless verifier; a centreline that carries no chain fails the call instead of stripping the rig on its way to a traceback. Flesh swing limits are suggested from a Godot measurement ladder, capped per flesh type so no suggestion lifts skin clear of the body, and a limit report that measured nothing is neither in_band nor settled and cannot be applied. Since 0.5.1 verify_strands reads the head's surface between the radius map's cells instead of from the nearest one, so a hair tie in the map no longer flips a penetration verdict by 2 cm. Since 0.5.2 the cloth skill says where a worn skirt or dress comes from: wardrobe.dress(body, preset, soft=True) builds it round the body and pins it at the hips, and Wardrobe.equip builds its SoftBody3D. Since 0.6.0 flesh.find_regions and prepare return a missed list naming each requested type that found no region and why (zone_empty, claimed by an earlier type, below_threshold, too_small, too_little) with the numbers against each threshold, summarize prints MISSED lines, all-NaN columns no longer warn, and verify_flesh.gd takes course=walk|run|jump (one motion alone, a jump held through its flight) and require= to choose which checks decide.

plugins.name: humanform
plugins.description: Adult human bodies in Blender, built in layers with a measured gate and a critic between every one, for Godot 4.7 and the plugins downstream of a body (rig-anything, follow-through, wardrobe, lookdev). A character brief - sex, age, stature, weight or build word, firmness, muscle, cupsize, skin - is resolved against ANSUR II, 6,068 measured adults as a multivariate normal per sex over 65 variables, by conditioning on what the brief fixes, so every measurement it does not name is the one people like that actually have. MPFB2 then builds the mesh and a Levenberg-Marquardt solve over its macros and fine targets fits it to those landmarks as humancheck measures them - joint heights, segment lengths, hand and foot, widths, and girths with their breadths and depths, because girth alone answered every waist with a pregnant belly. humancheck is the gate: it measures a body in its rig's rest pose against realistic or stylized presets, renders a fixed orthographic contact sheet in clay, normals and silhouette with target and measured landmark lines, and hands both to a critic subagent that writes its yes/no questions before it looks. humanlib makes it cheap to do again: a library of fitted bodies and judged parts indexed by ANSUR z-scores and critic-written tags, reuse in under a second, a warm start in a few seconds, faces, hands, feet and eyes as parts that move between bodies without stitching, and verdict statistics that steer later designs away from what critics reject. Since 0.6.2 eyes keep their face order between builds: Blender's create_uvsphere shuffles faces per process, which made every body the eyes were joined into differ. Since 0.6.3 the rigs it builds are tagged with the mpfb_game_engine profile, and the eyes take the head bone from it. Since 0.7.0 a body gets hair from a preset (short_crop, bob, bun, ponytail, long_loose): a feathered cap cut from the body's own faces with its boundary inside the texture's transparent root zone, coiled bun, tie and fall volumes, and a strand object follow-through springs. Muscle definition is a sculpted delta part weighted by the brief's muscle and estimated body fat, put on as geometry or baked into a normal map, with a facet guard that despikes the composite the mesh actually carries rather than each group alone. Since 0.7.1 the hair strand object carries ft_strand_type from its preset, so follow-through types a ponytail as a ponytail rather than reading it off the object's name. Since 0.8.0 pipeline.make takes fit_iterations and fit_detail for a cheaper, looser draft fit (defaults unchanged), and a draft fit is never stored in the library. Since 0.9.0 hair.add takes brows, lashes and body_hair (default off): humanform.brows adds brow cards (850 fine hairs) and upper and lower lash cards with their own tapering-hair texture, alpha scissor, transparent shadows and no Godot rim, backlight or anisotropy, in the hair colour darkened; and every hair cap is cut round the ears, so no cap strand covers an ear. Since 0.10.0 look.skin gives a body real skin (humanform.skin): regions marked as point attributes (lips, areolae, genital skin, knees, elbows and knuckles darker; palms and soles paler; flushed cheeks, nose and ears; oily T-zone), a flat Principled skin with subsurface until baked so an unbaked export still carries its tone, and on a game mesh a lookdev bake to albedo, ORM and normal maps with the albedo mean held to the brief within 0.03 sRGB plus an hf_detail UV for Godot pores; look.skin(..., realistic=False) keeps the old flat material.

plugins.name: wardrobe
plugins.description: Layered clothing for rigged Blender characters headed to Godot 4.7: a garment cut from the body it will be worn on, eased off the skin so the body never shows through, keeping the body's own skin weights (follow-through's jiggle bones included), with sprung bones around the hem and cuffs and a list of the skin it covers. In Godot one call moves the garment onto the body's skeleton, rebuilds the body without the covered triangles and springs the hem; a headless verifier walks the body and counts holes and skin through the cloth. Since 0.1.1 a fit is reproducible: every BVH is built from a canonical triangle order, so a body whose faces a join happened to shuffle still gives the same garment. Since 0.1.2 the rig map comes from rig-anything's bone roles when it is installed, with the name tables as the fallback, and hem bones are tagged wd_role. Since 0.2.0 garment presets (sports top, shorts, briefs, bra, trousers, T-shirt, long sleeve) hold the tailoring, ease, hem and cover arguments, dress() runs one onto a body over the layers under it, and cutting warns when the body's flesh is missing its jiggle weights. Since 0.2.1 the verifier counts a hole only where a viewer can see into the body: lines start at the skin, hidden skin off the cloth is looked at from 48 directions and reported occluded when nothing outside sees it, cloth pressed within 3 mm is reported coincident, cut= removes a patch of the garment as a control that must fail, and shot= renders a frame's holes. Since 0.2.2 a verifier run that measured nothing fails instead of passing: a clip=, body or garment that does not exist, setup cut short by a script error, or no sampled frame; still=true now samples the rest pose (it never did). Since 0.3.0 a compression garment is checked for what it traces: fit.relief is a surface's height over itself smoothed across 3 cm, so a nipple, a navel or a gluteal fold survives and the breast's own curve does not, and a detail_limit holds millimetres of the skin's relief the cloth carries through. A limited region that could not be measured is a problem and fails, instead of passing quietly. Since 0.4.0 skirts and dresses are opt-in presets (skirt_knee, skirt_mini, dress_sleeveless): a skirt is built round the body instead of cut from it, its 24 hem bones hang from the pelvis hinged just above the hip joints, and in Godot they fold with the thighs and swing out of thigh and shin capsules carried up to the hip; dress(..., soft=True) routes one to follow-through cloth instead, and the verifier counts cloth inside a thigh. Still open: at the top of a run stride the raised thigh shows through the front panel on some bodies, which no check counts yet. No existing preset changes. Since 0.5.0 the sports_top is a compression top on a heavy bust: its cloth spans the hollows under and between the breasts (ease span and span_radius: pushed out to its own hull only where a 10 cm ball cannot reach, never inward), settles over its own surface, keeps creased skin drawn (cover crease) and lifts smoothly over skin still drawn over it; on Belle the traced relief is 0.000 mm against the 0.060 mm limit, with no lift, no fold and no cloth edge bent over 35 degrees, and 21 of 21 verifier runs pass. dress reports sharp_edges and counts folded faces against their neighbours. The sports_top output changes on every body; it sits looser in the cleavage and under the bust. Other presets do not change.

plugins.name: character-pipeline
plugins.description: Build a whole character for Godot 4.7 from one TOML spec: a humanform body from a brief, baked, with hair, follow-through flesh, rig-anything's move set and wardrobe garments, exported as the glb, .moves.json and garment glbs MovesController and wardrobe.gd read. Stages know what they need and check the file before running, so garments before moves or flesh after garments refuse and name the order; each stage stores an input hash and its report on the rig, so a rebuild skips what has not changed and a fresh Blender session resumes from the saved .blend. Tuned numbers live in the plugins that own them - gait styles, flesh limit shares, garment presets - so a new character is a description, a style and an outfit, with no code. Since 0.2.0 height_m.stand is always the Idle clip's standing height (a spec naming export.height is refused), the manifest no longer carries upper_body, and the body report gives the body's measured stature. Since 0.3.0 the spec takes [hair] preset and colour and the hair stage builds it - hair joins into the body and nothing takes it off, so a file that already holds this character's hair is refused and told to rebuild from body - and a review stage renders rig-anything's review sheet after export, raising on a cell with no body in it or a body against an edge. Since 0.4.0 a ponytail spec keeps the tail loose and a strand stage between moves and garments hangs follow-through's strand chain on it; export writes <id>_hair.glb and lists strands in the manifest, and refuses while a strand mesh has no chain. long_loose stays joined and rigid. Since 0.5.0 a [muscle] section (output geometry or normal, strength, groups) runs humanform's muscle definition in a muscle stage between body and bake, the normal output baked into the skin's normal map; [build] quality (draft, preview, final) trades body fit, review and bake resolution for time, with a final build hashing as before; every build reports quality, per-stage seconds, skipped stages and total time in the report, the .blend and the manifest's build block; and a whole build whose [hair] or [muscle] changed, appeared or was dropped restarts from body instead of refusing. Since 0.6.0 the flesh stage prints what it found and what it missed with the numbers, fails when a type the spec names is missed unless [flesh] may_miss lists it, and the export writes a flesh block into .moves.json (per region type, bone, parent, peak_m, max_offset_m, material, frequency and damping, and the missed types with reason and whether allowed). Since 0.7.0 [hair] takes brows, lashes and body_hair switches (default false; a switch left false hashes as before, so no existing build restarts), passed to humanform 0.9.0 hair.add, and the hair stage reports the face layers it made. Since 0.7.1 the bake stage hash covers lookdev too, since humanform bakes the skin with it, so a lookdev release rebakes a stored skin.
